tagline: Your financial services advisor and provider of choice in each community we serve
hero_kpi_rationale: The Net Interest Margin is the primary profitability driver for a regional bank like Renasant, reflecting the spread between interest income generated from loans and the cost of deposits. It is a key structural performance indicator in the banking sector.

kpis.name: Net Interest Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between interest income from loans and the cost of deposits, expressed as a percentage of earning assets.
kpis.description: The net interest margin increased from 3.34% in 2024 to 3.79% in 2025, driven by the integration of The First's loan portfolio and improved rate dynamics.
kpis.signal: Margin on strong upward trend due to The First acquisition and organic loan growth.

kpis.name: Efficiency Ratio
kpis.explanation: Operating expenses divided by total revenues; the lower the ratio, the more efficient the bank.
kpis.description: The efficiency ratio deteriorated from 63.57% in 2024 to 65.00% in 2025, due to merger-related costs with The First.
kpis.signal: Slight deterioration in operational efficiency following the merger.

kpis.name: Return on Average Assets
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by average total assets, measuring the bank's overall performance.
kpis.description: ROAA declined from 1.11% in 2024 to 0.74% in 2025, due to higher credit loss provisions and integration costs.
kpis.signal: Decline in profitability despite asset growth.

kpis.short: Return on Average Tangible Common Equity
kpis.name: Return on Average Tangible Common Equity
kpis.explanation: Adjusted net income divided by average tangible common equity, a key metric for shareholders.
kpis.description: ROTCE dropped from 13.63% in 2024 to 9.65% in 2025, impacted by increased equity following the acquisition and higher provisions.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in shareholder profitability post-merger.

kpis.name: Provision for Credit Losses
kpis.explanation: Amount set aside to cover potential loan losses.
kpis.description: The provision for credit losses surged to $107,457 million in 2025 from $9,273 million in 2024, primarily due to the acquisition.
kpis.signal: Massive increase related to Day 1 provisioning from the merger with The First.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.explanation: Total value of assets held by the bank, a measure of size.
kpis.description: Total assets increased from $18,035 billion in 2024 to $26,751 billion in 2025, driven by the integration of $7,573 billion in assets from The First.
kpis.signal: Massive growth due to The First acquisition.

kpis.name: Loans Held for Investment
kpis.explanation: Total amount of loans originated by the bank, excluding loans held for sale.
kpis.description: The loan portfolio grew from $12,885 billion to $19,047 billion, with $5,173 billion coming from The First acquisition.
kpis.signal: Strong growth both organically and through acquisition.

kpis.name: Deposits
kpis.explanation: Total amount of customer deposits, the primary funding source for loans.
kpis.description: Deposits increased from $14,573 billion to $21,473 billion, supported by the acquisition and deposit gathering strategy.
kpis.signal: Growth in line with loans, with $6,449 billion acquired through The First.

kpis.short: Net Charge-offs as % of Average Loans
kpis.name: Net Charge-offs as % of Average Loans
kpis.explanation: Actual losses on defaulted loans, expressed as a percentage of average loans.
kpis.description: Net charge-offs increased from 0.06% in 2024 to 0.15% in 2025, reflecting a moderate deterioration in portfolio quality.
kpis.signal: Slight increase in defaults, but levels remain low.

kpis.name: Diluted EPS
kpis.explanation: Net income per share after dilution, a key metric for shareholders.
kpis.description: Diluted EPS declined from $3.27 in 2024 to $2.07 in 2025, due to integration costs and higher provisions.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline following a peak in 2024.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Credit risk on real estate loans
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the 10-K, with 75.10% of the portfolio in real estate, construction and commercial real estate loans. Language emphasizes the material impact of one or a few defaults. The Credit category is heavily weighted in the banking sector.

risks.title: Inadequate loan loss reserve
risks.score_rationale: The factor is repeated in detail, with mention of possible regulatory revisions and uncertainties in management estimates. Strong language: 'materially affect'. The Capital category is critical for banks.

risks.title: Interest rate risk
risks.score_rationale: Presented as a fundamental risk tied to net interest income. Mention of material effects on assets, liabilities and profitability. Language repeated and intensified by recent disintermediation events.

risks.title: Liquidity risk
risks.score_rationale: The risk is highlighted following the March 2023 bank failures. Text emphasizes dependence on deposits and increased competition. The Capital category is highly critical.

risks.title: Increased competition in the sector
risks.score_rationale: The factor is well developed, with mention of fintechs, lower costs among competitors and pricing pressure. Language indicating a material risk to profitability.

risks.title: Reliance on information provided
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly stated but with less alarmist language. It rests on potential errors in customer data. Less central than credit or liquidity risks.

risks.title: Persistent inflation risk
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned as an indirect but sustained factor. Impact on costs and customer purchasing power. Less direct than interest rate or credit risks.

ai_positioning.summary: Renasant Corporation does not mention any initiative, technology, or strategy related to artificial intelligence in its recent SEC filings. The focus remains on post-merger integration, credit risk management, and operational efficiency.
evidence: No mention of AI or machine learning technologies in the 10-K
Cited technology investments aim at improving operational capabilities, not AI innovation
No reference to predictive analytics tools, chatbots, or AI-based automation
